Every December I do the same exercise, and every December it hurts. I write down everything my team could do next year, and it is always about nine projects. Then I choose three. Not four. Three. The other six go on a second page called not this year, and I show that page to my director too, because he needs to see what we are not going to do. This year my three are retention in the stores, the leadership programme, and the new performance process. We are going to start with the store managers in April, because that is where the turnover is. The target is below twenty per cent by December. Will we get there? I do not know. But if I put nine projects on that page, I know exactly what will happen. Nothing.

Where do you see yourself in five years. Everybody hates this question, including me, and I still ask it. Not because I want a five year plan. I ask it because I want to know if you have a direction. The worst answer is the one that promises everything: I will be a director, I will lead a big team, I will change the company. The best answer is much smaller. Something like: I am going to keep working on culture, and in the next two years I want to do it in an international company, because that is the part I am missing. That tells me what you want and what you know about yourself. And one more thing for candidates who are not native speakers. Do not apologise for your English at the start of the answer. Just answer. If I need something repeated, I will ask.
My first priority is retention in the stores. We are going to start with the store managers in April. The target is below twenty per cent by December. I will send you the numbers on Monday.
